entries.title: Psalms 89:1
segments: This psalm may be viewed as an amplification of the ancient promise of God to David by Nathan,

, with a prayer that God would conform his dealings with his covenant people to it.  It plainly belongs to the later period of the Jewish history, when calamity upon calamity befell the kings of David's line, and with them the nation. 
 
The children of God, even in the deepest trials, have cause to sing of the mercies of the Lord, and praise him for his kindness to the sons of men.

entries.title: Psalms 89:2
segments:
Mercy--faithfulness; God's mercy and faithfulness to David and his seed. 
 
  Establish; make as permanent as the heavens.

entries.title: Psalms 89:3
segments: My chosen; applied to David, and through him to the Messiah, in whom the predictions of this psalm and many other psalms have their full accomplishment.

entries.title: Psalms 89:7
segments: God is to be adored with reverence and holy fear, as well as with confidence and filial affection.

entries.title: Psalms 89:9
segments: He who rules the waves of the sea is engaged for the protection of his people, and is able with perfect ease to control the movements of his and their enemies, and cause even their wrath to praise him and advance the good of his chosen.

entries.title: Psalms 89:10
segments: Rahab; Egypt, as a representative of the persecuting heathen powers.

entries.title: Psalms 89:12
segments:
Tabor; a mountain and city on the confines of Zebulun, in the north-east part of the plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Hermon; a mountain on the northern border of Palestine.

entries.title: Psalms 89:15
segments: The joyful sound; calling the people to the worship of God.

entries.title: Psalms 89:16
segments: If sinners are ever exalted, it must be, not on account of their own righteousness, but through the righteousness of God, which is unto and upon all that believe.

entries.title: Psalms 89:19
segments: To thy holy one; to David, and in David to Christ, in whom alone the promise has its perfect fulfilment.

entries.title: Psalms 89:20
segments: Anointed him; the holy oil by which David was consecrated to the kingly office was a symbol of the Holy Spirit, who came upon him from the day of his anointing,
; and who was given to Christ without measure at his baptism.

entries.title: Psalms 89:25
segments: His hand; his ruling hand.

entries.title: Psalms 89:27
segments: No earthly kings can be compared in excellence, dignity, honor, and glory with the Son of God.  He is the chief among ten thousand, altogether lovely, the brightness of Jehovah's glory, and the express image of his person, in whom dwells the fulness of the godhead bodily.

entries.title: Psalms 89:30
segments: His children; David's children, who occupied the earthly throne on Zion.

entries.title: Psalms 89:33
segments: Utterly take from him; by rejecting his house, as he did the house of Saul.

entries.title: Psalms 89:36
segments:
His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun; this is true of Christ and his people. 
 
The covenant of God with Christ, and through him with his people, is an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure.  Those who become interested in it, by the mighty power of God through faith unto salvation.

entries.title: Psalms 89:39
segments: Made void the covenant; as it seemed to the psalmist, but not in reality; for God's present dealings with the family of David were in accordance with the threatening contained in the original promise,
, repeated afterwards by David in his last charge to Solomon,
, and by God himself in a vision of Solomon,

entries.title: Psalms 89:40
segments: His hedges; the hedges which God had built around David and his kingdom.

entries.title: Psalms 89:47
segments: How short my time is; in view of the shortness of life and the approach of death, he beseeches God to manifest his loving-kindness, that life may not be filled with trouble and sorrow.  This thought is prominent in the book of Job.

entries.title: Psalms 89:48
segments: The time of man's continuance upon the earth must be short.  He should therefore do the work assigned him with fidelity, and in such a manner that when absent from the body he may be present with the Lord.

entries.title: Psalms 89:52
segments: Amen, and Amen; this doxology closes the third ancient division of the Psalms.
